title: Use My Numbers to Make Abstract SAT Problems Concrete
description: Recognize when variables can take many valid values, choose easy numbers that obey every condition, solve the concrete version, and test the answer choices with the same values.

questions.stem_html: A rectangle has width w and length 2 times its width plus 5 feet. Which expression gives its area in square feet?
questions.explanation_html: Choose w = 2. Then the length is 9 and the area is 18. Multiplying width times the stated length gives \(2w^{2}+5w\). Retest another legal width if any choices tie.
questions.variation: Choose legal lengths and test an expression for area

distractor_notes.A: Omits the width on the added length term.
distractor_notes.D: Swaps the roles of the scale and added length.

questions.stem_html: A club has x new members and 7 more returning members than new members. Which expression gives the total membership?
questions.explanation_html: If x = 9, returning members number 16 and the total is 25. In general the total is x + (x + 7) = \(2x+7\).
questions.variation: Build consistent counts and test a total expression

questions.stem_html: The ratio of red tiles to blue tiles is 3 to 5. Which expression gives the number of blue tiles when there are r red tiles?
questions.explanation_html: Choose 3 red tiles. There must be 5 blue tiles, giving 5/3 blue tiles per red tile. Scaling by r gives the expression.
questions.variation: Choose values that satisfy a ratio before comparing formulas

distractor_notes.B: Uses the whole group as the reference.
distractor_notes.C: Uses a constant difference for a ratio.

questions.stem_html: A shop takes 15% off a price p and then adds a fixed 6-dollar delivery fee. Which expression gives the final price?
questions.explanation_html: A convenient starting price is 100. The discounted price is 85, then the total is 91. The discount multiplies p by 85/100, and the fee is added afterward.
questions.variation: Use a base that makes percentages easy and verify both operations

distractor_notes.A: Adds the discount amount instead of the remaining amount.

questions.stem_html: A rectangle’s original length is l and its original width is w. The length is multiplied by 3 and the width by 5. Which expression gives the new area?
questions.explanation_html: For l = 3 and w = 2, the new area is 9 × 10 = 90. For any allowed l and w, (new length) × (new width) is \(15lw\).
questions.variation: Test a product relationship with two legal values
